mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% over the prior 6 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for at least 6 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite sustained FEDFUNDS > 5.25% for >6 months (p < 0.05 in a two-tailed test over the period)

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in a month, labor market strength anticipates a 5-day S&P 500 rally as investors price in accommodative policy and growth prospects.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp in a single month
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive months of UNRATE declines ≤0.15pp per month, with no significant positive 5-day SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05)

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP (PCE/GDP ratio) signals excess demand, which pushes up equity valuations and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PCE/GDPI ratio increases by >0.5 percentage points in a quarter
failure_condition: The PCE/GDPI ratio rise is not statistically significant (p > 0.10) or 60-day forward returns remain flat (mean 0%) across 5 such events

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply capacity, which tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during three such INDPRO contractions

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that prompt a 5-day S&P 500 decline as market anticipates rate hikes.
failure_condition: Over 20 such CPIAUCSL months, SPX 5-day returns are not consistently negative (average return ≥0%) or the Fama-French beta remains unchanged

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of 10% or more in a single month creates a momentum effect that drives a 60-day S&P 500 advance as investors reassess labor market resilience.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant positive 60-day SPX returns (p > 0.10) across 4 such events, or the effect is explained by idiosyncratic news (AQR IRN test p > 0.05)

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the given catalog but proxy via HOUST) exceeding prior month by >3% generate a 20-day S&P 500 upmove as demand momentum is priced in.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >3% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The HOUST pattern repeats but 20-day returns remain flat or negative (mean ≤0%) across 5 such events

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence (not directly observable; use as a regime indicator) coupled with two consecutive months of RSAFS < 700,000 suggests supply-side softness that precedes a 60-day S&P 500 decline.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 700,000 for two consecutive months AND confidence index falls (regime condition inferred from context)
failure_condition: During 3 such RSAFS < 700k regimes, SPX 60-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.10) or the effect is spurious (Granger causality fails)
